detail.text: Case gcd(n,k) = k is impossible and is proved in the partial: k | n, so q = n/k is prime and k*q = n divides k!, hence q <= k; with k*k <= n, q = k, so k is prime and k^2 | k!, i.e. k | (k-1)!, contradiction (about 15 lines, Nat.Prime.dvd_factorial, Nat.mul_dvd_mul_iff_left). The remaining case g = gcd(n,k) proper (g | k, 2 <= g <= k/2) gives n = g*q with q prime >= 2k, but I found no elementary contradiction: the weight is entirely in minFac C(n,k) > n/k >= k, i.e. no base-p borrow in n - k fo…
